title: Foundations & Forward: Ops, Hiring, and Risk Briefing
summary: Quarterly all-hands focused on operational foundations for scale: hiring cadence, incident posture, resourcing tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and a preview of the Q3 cost optimization program. Leadership answered questions about compensation bands, data residency roadmap, and upcoming product experiments. Next steps captured at the end.
next_steps: Priya to share hiring prioritization doc by 2026-08-05
Miguel to publish reliability playbook draft by 2026-08-12
Ava to start cross-team scoping for Optimize pilot next week
Leadership to schedule vertical breakouts in week of 2026-08-02
action_items: Priya: Create hiring prioritization doc, due 2026-08-05
Ava: Kick off Optimize pilot scoping, due 2026-08-07
Alex: Inventory on Dedicated capacity limits and region coverage, due 2026-08-03
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start time: 09:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (CEO), Ava (VP Product), Miguel (CTO), Priya (Head of People), Alex (Head of Infra), plus ~120 across the company (all-hands)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, good morning — thanks for joining the foundations and forward briefing. we'll try to keep this to an hour, we'll do updates from leadership then open to q and a. Quick note: if you have questions drop them in slack #all-hands-questions or use the Q&A widget.

[00:29] Ava: hi! super excited to run through product flags and the Optimize pilot. quick top line — Q3 is going to be about performance economics: lowering per-token costs on our hosted tier while continuing to keep latency SLAs for enterprise customers. some of this will be config improvements, some model routing work.

[01:05] Miguel: i'll cover reliability and infra changes. TL;DR: we're adding a second failover region for dedicated customers, and there's a change to our autoscale policy to reduce tail latency during bursts. we'll talk about tradeoffs in a minute.

[01:32] Priya: quick people note — hiring remains our bottleneck. we're prioritizing infra and sde roles, but also product engineering for Optimize. compensation line: we refreshed bands last week, total comp guidance will land to managers by friday.

[02:05] Alex: infra update: we've completed the PKI rotation for hosted control plane, thank you to the infra ops crew. rolling deploy for the new routing policy starts next tuesday.

[02:37] Sofia: ok, jumping to the agenda slide — first: hiring and org focus, second: incident posture and reliability, third: product ops and Optimize, fourth: private roadmap and compliance, then q and a.

[03:12] Ava: Hiring and product priorities — we have an intake of ~28 approved roles this quarter. prioritized list: 1) SREs (infra), 2) Backend infra engineers (k8s/serving runtime), 3) ML infra for KV/cache optimizations, 4) Product PMs for Optimize. We're going to experiment with a two-week 'coding + interview' blitz for critical roles.

[03:49] Employee (Speaker 1): question — will we be hiring internationally for infra roles?

[04:00] Priya: yes, we will expand hiring to EU and APAC for certain IC roles. comp ranges may vary by market; managers will get playbooks. visa support is still limited, prioritization will favor remote hires over sponsored relocation unless it's senior.

[04:28] Miguel: reliability posture — we're tracking three active reliability projects: A) second-region failover for dedicated pools, B) improved prefix caching consistency to reduce recompute during leader failover, C) better observability for per-request KV cache hits. The estimated impact: tail latency down 15-30% for large-sequence workloads.

[05:06] Alex: on the second-region plan, there's a capacity window issue for customers who pin to a single region — we're introducing a cross-region fallback lane for rapid failover but it will increase egress and a small bump in cost. We'll create a per-customer opt-in toggle for the first phase.

[05:41] Sofia: transparency here — for enterprise customers we will offer a config: strict single-region (lower egress cost) vs resilient multi-region (higher egress, better availability). 

[06:03] Employee (Speaker 2): are we communicating this change to sales and CSMs?

[06:12] Alex: yes, sales and CSMs get the config matrix and cost delta table next week.

[06:30] Ava: Optimize (cost/perf toolkit) preview — the pilot will focus on three levers: model selection + routing, quantization profile recommendations per workload, and cache/batch tuning suggestions. We'll run internal benchmarks and a small set of hosting customers in August.

[06:55] Miguel: technical note — Optimize will rely on our runtime meta-data layer, we need a few small infra hooks (per-tenant metrics and sequence-shape histograms). There will be a phased roll where the runtime emits extra signals; initial rollout won't affect default latency.

[07:24] Sofia: let's talk about private deployments and compliance — legal gave the green light to proceed with SOC 2 Type II audit prep; ISO work in parallel. There's also demand for an on-prem/hardened lite package for customers in regulated industries.

[07:50] Priya: a couple org notes — we're introducing a new 'on-call apprentice' program to broaden SRE coverage. this is a 6 week rotational program, not full pager responsibility, but gives exposure. Managers will nominate folks by 2026-08-05.

[08:17] Employee (Speaker 3): will apprentices be compensated differently?

[08:26] Priya: yes, small stipend and spot recognition; details in the doc i'll share.

[08:41] Sofia: moving to Q&A and open floor. we've collected questions, and we'll also take live ones. first pre-submitted: how are we thinking about pricing when Optimize reduces token usage?

[09:02] Ava: good question. pricing teams are modeling a couple outcomes: if Optimize reduces token spend via caching and routing, hosted revenue per request might decline; however, Optimize will be an addon (or tier) and we expect net retention to improve because customers can serve more throughput at predictable cost. We'll need to be careful with the economics of a free optimization that cannibalizes revenue.

[09:34] Employee (Speaker 4): will there be internal incentives for eng to participate in Optimize pilot?

[09:41] Sofia: yes, small bonuses for teams that meet pilot milestones; more importantly, career recognition — impact on cost is a major company KPI this quarter.

[09:58] Miguel: security and data residency — many customers asked about data-in-flight and at-rest keys. we validated KMS integrations for GCP and AWS; HSM vendors are in procurement evaluation. For private bundles, we'll add KMS+HSM configuration support in the next private release.

[10:25] Employee (Speaker 5): question on audit logging — will logs be available for customers?

[10:33] Alex: yes, audit logs are a part of the private package, and we're working on more granular retention policies. will push doc with sample log schemas.

[10:48] Sofia: ok, a transparency note for the company — we are forecasting a mid-year ramp in spend due to dedicated capacity commitments and hiring; we are balancing that with an aggressive cost optimization program. the goal is to keep runway healthy while investing in reliability and product-market fit.

[11:23] Employee (Speaker 6): are we expecting a hiring freeze if economic conditions worsen?

[11:31] Priya: not a freeze, more like a dynamic prioritization. we have triggers tied to net burn and bookings; if bookings fall below certain thresholds we recalibrate hiring. right now, we are green.

[11:48] Ava: quick demo snippet — Optimize dashboard mock (note: we referenced a deck, link in chat). It shows model routing suggestions, per-endpoint quantization profiles, and an ROI estimate. The ROI calc uses sequence-length distribution + cache-hit estimates.

[12:12] Miguel: technical caveat — model switching has to preserve semantic parity for high-sensitivity routes; we'll require eval sets and canary traffic to validate. This is not a blind switch.

[12:35] Employee (Speaker 7): what about the Dedicated autoscale change — will customers see slower scaling for cost reasons?

[12:44] Alex: no, scaling behavior for committed pools doesn't change; the policy we tweak affects burst lanes and throttle thresholds for pay-as-you-go slices to prevent double-spend scenarios in noisy neighbors. we'll post docs with scenarios.

[13:05] Sofia: we're going to do a short lightning round — each leader gives a one-minute ask from the company. Ava?

[13:12] Ava: ask — if you work on any thing touching the runtime, add one test-case that exercises KV cache behavior for long sequences. helps with the prefix caching work.

[13:27] Miguel: ask — if you see flaky telemetry or dashboards, create an incident and tag infra-signal slack channel; please include a link to the trace.

[13:41] Priya: ask — managers please confirm headcount plans in the hiring sheet by monday.

[13:49] Alex: ask — infra folks, sign up for the cross-region dry run on 2026-08-10.

[14:02] Sofia: closing notes — we'll break into vertical-themed AMAs next week, signups are in the calendar. remember the leadership office hours on thursday for any follow-ups. thank you.

[14:23] Live Q&A (selected):
[14:26] Employee (Speaker 8): Can we get more detail on the compensation band refresh?
[14:33] Priya: short answer: bands moved up ~6% avg, overlap between levels tightened. managers get detail and calibration guide friday.

[14:50] Employee (Speaker 9): How are we prioritizing private on-prem customers vs hosted growth?

[14:57] Sofia: both — hosted is our growth engine, private is strategic for larger deals. we staff a small dedicated team for private while continuing to iterate on hosted. prioritization is deal-driven and ROI-driven.

[15:20] Employee (Speaker 10): what's the cadence for reliability incident follow ups?

[15:28] Miguel: postmortems within 72 hours, remediation action plan within two weeks. we'll publish the reliability scorecard monthly.

[15:44] Employee (Speaker 11): will we open source any parts of Optimize?

[15:51] Ava: open to selective OSS components (metrics emitter, evaluation harness) but the policy and recommendations engine will likely remain internal initially.

[16:08] Sofia: final wrap — we'll send the deck, the hiring prioritization sheet, and the Optimize pilot charter to the company. leadership office hours and vertical breakouts details coming in calendar invites.

[16:26] Sofia: thanks team, meeting adjourned.

[16:45] Post-meeting quick notes (auto-generated): Summary: leadership presented the Q3 operational priorities. Action items created. Follow-ups scheduled for next two weeks.

End of transcript.
